Headline
The three notes now pass the checks, and the procedure is in notes/procedure.md.
The parser note drops the booster and keeps the two-second claim.
The incident note splits one long sentence into three facts.
The design note drops the booster and splits the worker steps.

Background
Three notes failed the checks for banned words and long sentences. The request asks for a procedure any agent can follow, then a fix of notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md in that order. Each file must keep its meaning.

Relevance
A later agent can repeat the same steps without a new design. The notes are ready to read because the checks now report no failures.

Information
check_file on notes/a.md first reported the booster "clearly" and no sentence over 25 words. The rewrite removes that word. The speed claim and the two-second log claim stay.

check_file on notes/b.md first reported one sentence over 25 words and no banned word. It also reported a grade over 10. The rewrite splits the outage, the database fallback, and the one-hour end into three sentences. The facts stay the same.

check_file on notes/c.md first reported the booster "very" and one sentence over 25 words. The rewrite drops "very" and splits the worker steps. The queue behavior stays the same.

A second check_file on each file reports zero sentences over 25 words and no banned words. Failures are empty for all three files.

Assumption: the 25-word check is the sentence limit that check_file enforces. Why not measured: the tool reports sentences over 25 words, not a separate 20-word count. Validate by: run check_file after each rewrite. If wrong: split any sentence the tool still flags.

Alternative considered: keep one sentence per file and only swap banned words. That loses because notes/b.md and notes/c.md fail the length check until the sentences are split.

End
I recommend that we keep notes/procedure.md as the shared steps. Next, leave notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md as rewritten, because the second checks pass. Then use the same seven steps on any later notes file before you publish it.

arguments.content:
# Procedure: fix banned words and long sentences

Any agent can follow these steps for one notes file. The tools are `list_files`, `read_file`, `check_file`, and `write_file`.

1. Call `list_files` and confirm the target path exists in the sandbox.
2. Call `read_file` on that path and keep the full text.
3. Call `check_file` on that path and record each banned word and each sentence over 25 words.
4. Rewrite the file in full. Keep the meaning. Replace each banned word with a plain word that does not boost, hedge, or praise. Split each sentence over 25 words so every sentence has 25 words or fewer. Use active voice. Keep one topic per paragraph.
5. Call `write_file` with the full new text. This replaces the old content.
6. Call `check_file` again. If it still reports a banned word or a sentence over 25 words, repeat steps 4 to 6. Stop when `check_file` reports none.
7. Call `read_file` and compare the new text with the old text. Confirm the facts and the request stay the same.

Do these steps for one file before you start the next file.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started when the cache filled up during the nightly import. The service then used the database for every request. This lasted until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue is simple. Each worker takes one message and runs the job. It writes the result to the store. It then marks the message as done so no other worker takes it again.
